title: Narrative AI and adaptive games
author: ChocolateTemporary48
selftext:
First, let me explain what I’m referring to.



I see a lot of brilliant ideas around here regarding various games—as well as some superficial ones, though that’s to be expected.



However, I notice that the potential of LLMs to act as narrators and interpreters remains largely unexplored.



A well-adapted and fine-tuned LLM could serve as a decent narrator for certain types of games where player choices truly matter, allowing for far greater flexibility.



I don’t know how many of you have tried setting up a role-playing scenario using JSON for save data and Python for deterministic systems, but even with fairly basic setups, some really interesting things tend to happen.



It’s true that this field is still in its infancy; there are plenty of attempts out there, but they often fail to solve specific problems or prove too costly.



Still, I see this becoming increasingly common over the next decade, and I’m genuinely hopeful about it—games that truly feel alive and react to your wildest ideas.

comments.author: SurvivalHermit
comments.body: The value i see in LLMs is they are non deterministic. Games (especially MMO and ARPG games) take in a lot of data about the players. What they kill how they kill it where they go all kinds of things. This data can be fed into an LLM to output simple changes to databases that control spawns and behavior of NPCs and enemies and environments and all kinds of things. The reason this is so valuable is because the LLM will not always make the exact same decisions even provided the exact same data so it is difficult (moreso the more data points you provide) to ever "solve" the process to get the outcome. One of the most immersion breaking things in MMO games today is the redundancy. An LLM can solve that without having to make more than a few calls an hour and ask it to interpret some player gameplay data.

replies.author: ChocolateTemporary48
replies.body:
When I speak of determinism, I’m referring to basic, general data—such as a crossbow's armor-piercing capability or a character's funds.



If it’s something more along the lines of a 4X game, it would be the resources your empire manages.



It’s a combination of those factors and the LLM acting as the final interpreter, depending on the situation.



Nowadays, there are highly capable, ultra-cheap models like DeepSeek 4.1 Flash; I can only imagine what it will be like in a couple of years when the AGI era begins.



Cost and tokens per second will no longer be an issue.
